correctness.rationale: For any connected subset C of the orbit set, the first coordinate is fixed. If the nth projection of C is the singleton {a}, then the (n+1)st projection is a connected subset of the totally disconnected fiber F(a), hence is a singleton; induction forces C itself to be a singleton. Nondegeneracy lets any orbit be changed after an arbitrarily long common prefix, so there are no isolated points. Upper semicontinuity gives closedness in the compact metrizable product. These three facts yield the Cantor characterization.
